items.text: Greetings, everyone!

Despite our best efforts, the update we've released last week was not completely without issues. However, thanks to your vigilance and detailed feedback, we've already been able to catch and dispose of several pesky bugs, and even bring other highly requested improvements and changes with this latest patch:
Fixed Crash when getting the Yellow Keycard in MedBay
Fixed falling through Platforms in the The Eye
Changed the fog in The Eye for better frame rate
Further rebalanced enemy audio
Added screen fade behind inventory screen and datapad
Changed the location for tool tips on the inventory screen
Added Exclamation markers to the Reactor Puzzle in Level 1 to make it easier
Changed font for Messages, Dialogue, and Weapon Wheel to a more readable font for English

And of course, our work doesn't stop there - if you wish to help us make HYPERVIOLENT the best game it can be, please report any bugs or technical issues and share any suggestions for how to improve the game - either here in the comments, in the Steam Discussions, or on the Fulqrum Publishing Discord server . And if you enjoy HYPERVIOLENT and want to support the game further, please, consider writing a positive review (recommendation) here on Steam - it really helps us and energizes us to keep the updates coming.
Greetings, everyone!

We have a big update for you today! Thanks to your feedback, we have added several quality of life improvements, such as a new option for killed enemies to drop loot on the ground instead of having to rummage through corpses' inventories, better balanced lighting and improvements to inventory management and UI readability, among many others. We have also squashed numerous pesky bugs and crashes, especially those related to the inventory system.
Before you jump off to browse those deals, or just skip down to the full list of changes and fixes at the end of this article, a few words from the developer himself:

"Thank you to everyone who has played HYPERVIOLENT so far. I really appreciate all of the feedback I’ve received. HYPERVIOLENT definitely does not play like most other games in the genre, and this may have taken some players by shock initially, but I am dedicated to ironing out the experience for players who appreciate the game’s slower, more nuanced take on the retro shooter genre."

nfoPRINCE: As you can see, we are commited to keep working on the game and supporting it with further patches. If you find any bugs, technical issues or have any suggestions for how to improve the game, please, share them with us here in the comments, in the Steam Discussions, or come to the Fulqrum Publishing Discord server . And if you enjoy HYPERVIOLENT and want to support the game further, please, consider writing a positive review (recommendation) here on Steam - it really helps us and energizes us to keep the updates coming.
Added a floodlight to the Personal Transport Vessel, per player feedback.

Added a quicker "Take All Items" button to the loot screen. This will indiscriminately take items and will not remove ammunition from weapons; the player can still choose to do that manually during looting or in their inventory.

Added an option for "Auto-Drop Loot." This can be turned on or off at any time and causes enemies to drop their items on the ground at death. Drop rates are exactly the same. This removes the looting process but gives a more classic shooter feel.
The generic cursor is now the default for UI instead of the red gloved hand.
Fixed numerous crashes related to the inventory.
Improved inventory alignment when placing and picking up items.
It is now more obvious when the player is discarding an item from their inventory.
Improved gamepad control for the inventory.
Improved gamepad sensitivity; the player can now look around at a more reasonable speed.
Fixed a crash that occurred if the player died while looting a corpse.
Fixed issues with the player falling through the floor after leaving the Personal Transport Vessel.
Fixed numerous broken achievements.
Fixed slowdown related to blood splatters when striking enemies with projectile weapons.
Fixed issues where the player could fall out of the Engineering Level during low gravity.
Fixed an issue where the game did not auto-save after the Valentine Mech boss fight.
Fixed an issue where the player would inadvertently use health items or grenades while looting (gamepad).
Fixed the item duplication and item vanishing glitch near the edge of the inventory screen.
Rebalanced lighting for the entire game, removing total darkness. Even without the flashlight, the player now has some limited visibility.
Improved font style for much of the UI to be more readable.
Rebalanced the shotgun to make it more powerful.
Rebalanced some enemy alert sounds.
Rebalanced the HMG; it now fires faster.
Improved overall game performance on most machines. (Laptops with external displays may still have slowdown issues; we are still working on this.)
Rebalanced drop tables for loot again based on player feedback (more ammo, especially in later levels, and fewer health items).
Hello Everyone!

We have just released the update that was previously accessible through a beta - we are grateful to all of you who participated and shared your feedback. Thanks to you, everyone can now enjoy it and use the new options the update brings.

We are commited to keep working on the game and supporting it with further patches. If you find any bugs, technical issues or have any suggestions for how to improve the game, please, share them with us here in the comments, in the Steam Discussions, or come to the Fulqrum Publishing Discord server . And if you enjoy HYPERVIOLENT and want to support the game further, please, consider writing a positive review (recommendation) here on Steam - it really helps us and energizes us to keep the updates coming.

notes.title: Full Change Log of the v1.0.0.3 update

items.text: Yellow Nanocard crash no longer happens, and it should be possible to continue playing from the affected save files
Weapon, Ammo and health vial drops rebalanced
1440p resolution added

Post processing can be disabled from the "options => graphics" menu for bloom, grain, and depth of field. Disabling bloom should fix the issue with overly bright light sources some players have reported.
Dialogue for Russian language no longer cuts off early.
Tutorial typos have been corrected, and the tutorial no longer waits too long to go to the next section.
Green LMG Zombie's Alert sound volume has been decreased and tweaked
Hello Everyone!

We are working hard on a patch with various fixes and tweaks based on your reports; most notable, the fix to the game-breaking bug happening when you find the yellow nanocard. And while the updated version shows promise, thorough testing is still required before its full release. Your help with this process would be invaluable, that's why the new update has been made available as an open beta here on Steam.

If you do decide to give it a go, first of all - huge thanks! And second, if you run into any issues, please report them either here in the comments, in Steam Discussions, or come to the Fulqrum Publishing Discord server and let us know there. Just specify that the report you're making is for the open beta.

To access the beta branch, head to your Steam Library, right-click HYPERVIOLENT, left-click Properties, left-click Betas and from the drop-down menu select the option "update_beta". Your game will then update to the desired version.
You can find the following fixes and changes in the update beta:
Yellow Nanocard crash no longer happens, and it should be possible to continue playing from the affected save files
Weapon, Ammo and health vial drops rebalanced
1440p resolution added
Post processing can be disabled from the menu for bloom, grain, and depth of field.
Dialogue for Russian language no longer cuts off early.
Tutorial typos have been corrected, and the tutorial no longer waits too long to go to the next section.
Green LMG Zombie's Alert sound volume has been decreased and tweaked
Hello everyone!

It is with great excitement that as a part of the Lovecraftian Days event, we bring you a surprise Content Update #3 for HYPERVIOLENT. We know that you have waited patiently, through our rocky development roadmap, and we'd like to thank you with this bonus content.

This update to the game addresses numerous bugs, performance issues, community suggestions (such as controller support, higher resolutions), and provides more depth to the game's immersive-sim mechanics.

Before we fully launch the content update to the public, though, we will open a beta branch on Steam where the update will be available to play for anyone who owns HYPERVIOLENT. The reason we're doing this is to make sure the build with the current update is stable and contains no major issues. After we're sure it's good to go, we'll update the public branch with the current update too.

To access the beta branch, head to your Steam Library, right-click HYPERVIOLENT, left-click Properties, left-click Betas and from the drop-down menu select the option "update_beta". Your game will then update to the desired version. We can't wait to hear what you think!
The whole list of changes and additional content can be found below the article.
The lead developer has also prepared a personal statement regarding the game's upcoming full release that he'd like to share with you.

"Greetings, HYPERVIOLENT fans and critics alike. I wanted to take a few moments to thank each and every one of you for your continued support, feedback, and interest in this passion project of mine. What started as a small billboard sprite experiment in 2018, has taken on a life of its own, with now thousands of people exploring its haunted corridors in search of answers for what really happened on Commodus Asteroid 27-C. Firstly, let's address the roadmap. The game has now been in Early Access for a little less than two years, which is behind schedule, and in that time, I've learned alot about what the community expects, and exactly how difficult it can be to develop a full-blown indie game. As we leave Early Access in the coming months, I will be a lot more active in the Fulqrum Discord, and in the Steam Discussion forums, answering questions and taking feedback.

Some people have pointed out apparent development inactivity in the year of 2024, and while we never stopped developing, there were definitely reasons for the slowdown. I experienced the sudden loss of both of my parents, as well as the death of a close-friend and frequent collaborator on the game itself at the end of the year. During this time we also restructured our studio, resulting in HYPERVIOLENT now being finished under the nfoPRINCE banner, one formed especially for this game.
Stay tuned.”
Daniel K

items.text: Hello everyone,

It's been a little over a week since we have released the long-awaited second Content Update, with a new level, whole new spaceship flying and combat mechanic and more. What do you think about it, are you enjoying the brand-new way to experience the horrific atmosphere of HYPERVIOLENT? Please let us know either here in the comments, Steam Discussions, or on the Fulqrum Publishing Discord server!
And for those who have not yet had a chance to play the new content, we have prepared a gameplay trailer for the new level, Viscera of Commodus:

We are now working on finalizing the content for the full launch of the game - new levels, new weapons, more story/lore elements, full localization to German, Simplified Chinese and Russian languages, and more! But in the meantime, we are of course on the lookout for any bug reports and feedback on balancing and other aspects of the game - if needed, we will produce patches before the full launch.

We truly appreciate all your support, and humbly ask for a little more patience - while we do not expect finalizing the upcoming content will take as long as preparing the new mechanics did, we are committed to bringing you an engaging and balanced gameplay experience as well as gripping story with the full launch of HYPERVIOLENT.
And we have heard you - we will do our best to provide you with more information about the progress of development moving forward.
Hello everyone!
It is with utmost pleasure that we finally bring you the second Content Update for HYPERVIOLENT!

It took more time than we expected, as we ran into some issues in develpment, and we humbly apologize for that. But here we are, serving you what we promised and we hope you like it - and to give you an idea of what awaits you, let's watch a new trailer!

Please, let us know what you think, whether it's the Content Update itself or the main game. The best place to share your feedback would be the discussion forum here on Steam, so don't hesitate to let us know what you think! The whole Change Log can be found below.

It is also important to mention that saves that you created before downloading this Content Update will not be compatible with the current build. This is, sadly, necessary for the game to work properly.
And if you don't have enough, check out the rest of the BOOMSTOCK 2024 event participants, as there are many great games running discounts, showing new trailers, adding new content or even launching!
Level 7 Viscera of Commodus
True 6-degree of freedom ship flying mechanic and combat
1 new weapon Arc Rifle
3 new enemies Small-Drone, Medium-Drone, Legion-Drone
